title: Press conference: Wings in Nashville | 1974
content:
Wings held a press conference in Nashville, Tennessee, on 17 June 1974.

It came just hours before the band’s guitarist Jimmy McCulloch was arrested and jailed for reckless driving. He was released shortly afterwards and returned to England on 18 July.

The conference was held at the farm in which Wings stayed during their Nashville period. Owned by songwriter Claude ‘Curly’ Putman Jr, it was rented for $2,000 a week by the band, who rehearsed in the garage.

The event was deliberately low-key, with Paul McCartney sitting in a rocking chair on the front porch, Linda and drummer Geoff Britton nearby, and local reporters stationed on the steps and lawn below.

At the time, the McCartneys were unsure of the future of Wings, and were considering jettisoning McCulloch and Denny Laine. Asked about McCulloch’s run-in with the law, McCartney confirmed it had happened. “Yeah, I think so, yes. But I’d rather not talk about it.”

Following the conference, the McCartneys posed for photographs, after which they held a full band meeting for four hours.

That evening an overdub session was held at the Sound Shop Studio for Denny Laine’s song ‘Send Me The Heart’. It was the band’s final work in Nashville, and they left the following day.
